newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Palestinian official calls for EU peace role.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian official calls for EU peace role.

text.p: A senior Palestinian official on Tuesday urged the European Union to play a direct role in the stalled Middle East peace process and use its economic influence to step up pressure on Israel.
Hanan Ashrawi, a minister in the Palestinian National Authority and a member of the legislature, said she hoped to strengthen EU-Palestinian ties during a three-day visit to Austria.
"There is a very strong role to be played by Europe, whether on a bilateral level or collectively as a European Union," she told reporters at a news briefing.

Europe should use its economic clout in the region to influence Israel, she said. "I'm not saying we should go as far as sanctions, but I think there are a lot of powers of persuasion to be exercised in different ways," she added.
Israel has long opposed a European presence in the negotiations because of Europe's political and economic involvement in the Middle East.
Ashrawi said she had discussed Austrian support for the peace process during a meeting with Benita Ferrera-Waldner, state secretary at the Austrian Ministry for Foreign affairs.
"I had a sense that Austria really would like to be more active politically for the peace process and that they will do that bilaterally and also within the EU," she said.
Ashrawi said the current Israeli government under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had destroyed the credibility of the peace process and threatened Arab-Israeli relations.

"Now is the time to stand up and speak out," she urged. "The Netanyahu government has to understand it cannot dictate its will to the rest of the world. It cannot decide to alter the course of history unilaterally."
She cited a recent visit of French President Jacques Chirac to Israel, during which he confronted heavy-handed Israeli police, as a breakthrough in EU-Arab relations.
"He stood up and broke many of the taboos. It was a refreshing reminder that Israel is not above accountability," she said.
